label: weak, diffuse: around <DEL> / first copy outputs, biased to sequences starting with 0/c/2/u
explanation: Sparse (~1% of steps) and diffuse. Its strongest firing is at the <DEL> step (4.7x lift, 40% of mass) and at the first copy step (recall_idx 1, 2.4x), more so for long sequences (L 8-9) and when the first original token, which is output right after <DEL>, is 0/c/2/u. It also fires on inputs u/e/2/h in any phase, but only at 3-5% rate. Top activations are <DEL> followed by first output 2/0/u. No predicate tried got past F1 0.18 (delimiter alone: P 0.05, R 0.36; inputs {u,e,2,h,DEL}: R 0.79 but P 0.04). Activation looks like a dense function of sequence history that the tested variables do not capture. Never fires at t=0 and rarely at t=1.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output, by phase (delimiter step: 0, c, 2, q; copy phase: 0, c, t, 1; input phase: ) and the current input token, by phase (copy phase: u, 2, w, o; input phase: e, h, b, r; delimiter step: <DEL>); timing cues that raise it most: L=9 & t=10, L=3 & t=2, L=8 & t=9.
